messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 PAGE: silverlake-prod (private) - Auth failures for tenant silverlake-finance on silverlake-dedicated-us-east-2. Error: OIDC token validation failed (invalid_signature). Paging oncall. :rotating_light:
ashok (oncall): Got the page, I'm on it. Assigning @elena and @james. Any evidence of certificate expiry or JWKS mismatch?
silverlake-sre: Hey team — started seeing 401s around 10:03 UTC. Clients hitting our VPC endpoint get `invalid_signature` from token verifier. No deployments on our side. We did a scheduled IDP key rotation ~09:50 but vendor said it was backward compatible.
elena (infra): Thanks. Which verifier is failing? Is this our OIDC middleware (tenant-verify) or the dedicated pool's proxy?
james (sre): Logs from the dedicated proxy show repeated failures when validating tokens:```text
2026-03-14T10:03:12Z token=eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6IjEyMyJ9... error=signature_verification_failed kid=456
2026-03-14T10:03:14Z token=... error=signature_verification_failed kid=456
```
james (sre): The kid in the tokens (456) is not present in the cached JWKS we have for silverlake's idp. Our JWKS cache timestamp: 2026-03-14T09:40Z.
tess (cs): Customer reports degraded traffic affecting 30% of requests. They are on a financial batch window. High business impact. They asked for ETA and workaround.
ashok (oncall): Ok, immediate mitigation options: 1) Force refresh JWKS from customer idp 2) Allow a temporary fallback to `allow_unvalidated_tokens` for non-sensitive routes (not preferred) 3) Ask customer to push the new public key to their idp with previous kid alias.
silverlake-sre: We can re-publish the JWKS to a static URL if needed. IdP vendor said the new key has kid=456 and should have been in the JWKS but propagation failed to some edge caches.
ryan (eng-runtime): I'll try a forced JWKS fetch and hot reload for the dedicated pool. Commands I will run on the console:```bash
# force-refresh JWKS for tenant silverlake
redwoodctl tenants refresh-jwks --tenant silverlake --pool silverlake-dedicated-us-east-2
# reload proxy config
redwoodctl pools reload-config --pool silverlake-dedicated-us-east-2
```
ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered: refresh-jwks job queued (job id: refresh-789).
ashok (oncall): Run it, and let's watch logs. If that doesn't work, we may need to accept a one-off manual JWKS upload to our control plane.
ryan (eng-runtime): Running refresh now. Logs:```text
[10:07:02] refresh-jwks start tenant=silverlake job=refresh-789
[10:07:05] https://idp.silverlake.example/.well-known/jwks.json fetched, size=3 keys
[10:07:05] key kid=123 present, kid=789 present, kid=456 present
[10:07:06] cache updated, propagating to 4 regional proxies
```
james (sre): Proxy logs now show successful verifications for previously failing tokens. Example:```text
2026-03-14T10:07:12Z token=... kid=456 status=verified
```
ashok (oncall): Silverlake, can you confirm customer traffic recovers on your end?
silverlake-sre: We're seeing successful auth on ~90% of new requests. Some long-lived clients still failing — looks like client-side caching of tokens with old kid? We're advising session refresh.

tess (cs): Customer asked: why did this happen if vendor said it's backward compatible? They want a post-incident summary and a mitigation for next rotation.
elena (infra): Root cause hypothesis: vendor rotated signing key and issued tokens with new kid before JWKS propagated to all vendor CDN edges; their rotation TTL was short. Our JWKS fetcher had a 30-minute TTL and a stale cached value in some regional proxies (cache not invalidated by rotation). Combined, tokens with new kid hit our region before cache refresh.
ryan (eng-runtime): Follow-ups: - Reduce JWKS cache TTL for private tenants to 60s on rotation detection - Add on-demand JWKS pull when signature validation fails for unknown kid - Add metrics/alert when token-kid-mismatch rate > 1% per minute
james (sre): We've left refresh-789 in place and propagation completed to all active proxies. I'll keep monitoring.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1534 (SEV2) assigned to ashok, sla: 4h, priority: high.
ashok (oncall): Handoff plan: @elena own infra changes (TTL + on-demand pull). @ryan own runtime metrics + hotfix. @james keep monitoring and draft customer comms with @tess. I will stay until customer confirms full recovery.
silverlake-sre: Thank you. We'll coordinate a controlled key rotation window with vendor and share pre-rotation checks.
tess (cs): Customer impact note for postmortem: "30% auth failures for 20m during vendor key rotation; partial recovery after forced JWKS refresh; residual client cache issues."
elena (infra): Temporary mitigation checklist committed:```yaml
- set jwks_cache_ttl: 60s for tenant:silverlake
- enable on_demand_jwks_fetch_on_unknown_kid: true
- add monitor: token_kid_mismatch_rate > 0.01 -> pager
```
ryan (eng-runtime): I'll open an RFC for behavior on unknown kid (fallback strategies) and schedule a minor release.
james (sre): Closing tasks for now: monitoring OK, customer reports degraded sessions clearing. I'll mark incident as mitigated and start draft.
ashok (oncall): Great job team. After-action: please capture timelines and actionable items in INC-2026-1534. I'll hand off to next oncall in 30m. :thumbsup:
